source_evidence.observation: The exercise fixes a standard normal random variable g with distribution N(0,1) and asks for a statement valid for every real t≥1.
The source states E[g^2 1_{g>t}] = t(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) + P{g>t} ≤ (t+1/t)(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2).
The source's proof hint is: 'Integrate by parts.'

binders: g is a real-valued standard normal random variable with distribution N(0,1) on an implicit probability space (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 opening sentence).
t is a real threshold universally quantified over t≥1 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 phrase 'for all t ≥ 1').
hypotheses: g has the standard normal distribution N(0,1) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 opening sentence).
conclusions: E[g^2 1_{g>t}] = t(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) + P{g>t} (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed equality).
t(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) + P{g>t} ≤ (t+1/t)(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed inequality).
definitions_and_conventions: N(0,1) denotes the standard normal distribution (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 opening sentence).
1_{g>t} denotes the indicator of the strict upper-tail event {g>t} (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
E[g^2 1_{g>t}] is the second moment of g truncated to the event g>t (PDF page 4/printed page 15, exercise title and displayed formula).
P{g>t} is the probability of the strict upper-tail event (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) is the standard normal density evaluated at t (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
The final factor is exactly t+1/t multiplying the complete density expression (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed inequality).
implicit_context: The equality and upper bound are both required parts of the exercise (PDF page 4/printed page 15, the chained equality and inequality in the single display).
The event is written with the strict comparison g>t in both the indicator and probability term (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
The endpoint t=1 is included, and t≥1 ensures that the denominator in 1/t is nonzero (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 threshold condition and displayed bound).
The result is an exact identity followed by an exact inequality, not an asymptotic statement (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 display).
The hint 'Integrate by parts' supplies proof guidance but does not add a hypothesis or conclusion (PDF page 4/printed page 15, hint following the exercise).
The subsequent Section 2.2 material on Hoeffding's inequality is outside this exercise's task boundary (PDF page 4/printed page 15, structural boundary after the hint).

details: The integrand is g squared times the indicator of {g>t}, not g, |g|, or a conditional expectation (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
The truncation is to the strict upper tail only (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 displayed formula).
The boundary-density contribution is exactly t(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed equality).
The remaining term is exactly P{g>t}, added to the boundary-density contribution (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed equality).
The right-hand prefactor is exactly t+1/t (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed inequality).
The normalization and decay factor are exactly 1/sqrt(2π) and exp(-t^2/2) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed inequality).
The inequality is non-strict and valid for every t≥1 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, exercise statement and display).
The only stated hint is to integrate by parts (PDF page 4/printed page 15, hint immediately following Exercise 2.1.4).
The source does not specify in the hint the precise integral representation, choice of factors, or boundary-term calculation (PDF page 4/printed page 15, terse hint 'Integrate by parts').

undebatable_constraints: The random variable g has distribution N(0,1) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 opening sentence).
The threshold domain is every real t≥1, including t=1 (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 statement).
The truncated quantity is exactly E[g^2 1_{g>t}] (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed formula).
The tail event is the strict event {g>t} in both the indicator and probability (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed formula).
The exact identity is E[g^2 1_{g>t}] = t(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) + P{g>t} (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed equality).
The exact upper bound is E[g^2 1_{g>t}] ≤ (t+1/t)(1/sqrt(2π))exp(-t^2/2) (PDF page 4/printed page 15, chained display).
The constants 1/sqrt(2π), the exponent -t^2/2, and the prefactor t+1/t must be preserved exactly (PDF page 4/printed page 15, displayed formula).
Both the equality and inequality are required; neither may be omitted (PDF page 4/printed page 15, chained display).
The stated proof hint is integration by parts (PDF page 4/printed page 15, hint following the exercise).
No Hoeffding, Bernoulli, MGF, or neighboring Section 2.2 claim belongs to this exercise contract (PDF page 4/printed page 15, structural boundary after the hint).

ambiguities.issue: The integration-by-parts hint does not specify the exact integral setup.
ambiguities.evidence: PDF page 4/printed page 15 gives only the two-word hint 'Integrate by parts.'
ambiguities.impact: A formal proof must choose an integral representation and justify its boundary terms, but this does not make the mathematical statement ambiguous.

contract_plain_english: If g is standard normal, then for every t≥1 its second moment restricted to the strict upper tail satisfies the exact identity E[g^2 1_{g>t}] = t exp(-t^2/2)/sqrt(2π) + P{g>t}, and this is at most (t+1/t)exp(-t^2/2)/sqrt(2π). The source suggests proving it by integration by parts (PDF page 4/printed page 15, Exercise 2.1.4 and its hint).
